artworks.title: Elisa H. Hamilton: Heirlooms
artworks.description: Heirlooms presents a vibrant series of abstract works on paper featuring joyful color palettes, lyrical linework, and dynamic geometric patterns. This body of work draws its essence from a handcrafted quilt made by Hamilton’s great-grandmother, passed down to the artist by her father. Hamilton’s paintings create a dialogue across generations, using her unique visual language to transform family stories into vivid contemporary abstractions. Through delicate layers of gouache and bold swaths of black gesso, Hamilton celebrates how family artifacts are capable of carrying our most enduring memories.

artworks.title: Discover Ancient Egypt (temporarily closed)
artworks.description: Designed to appeal to school groups and families, this interactive gallery introduces visitors to the wonders of one of the oldest and most accomplished civilizations in recorded history. Realistic paintings of ancient tomb walls —painted on-site by celebrated painter Joseph Lindon Smith in the 1920s and ‘30s, and on loan from the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston— bring both the history and art of ancient Egypt to life. In addition, visitors will see murals depicting Egyptian religious beliefs, small sculptures, everyday objects, a miniature diorama about mummification, and hands-on activity stations. “Our goal was to make the gallery educational, interactive, and fun,” says Laura Howick, Director of Education Emeritus. Try de-coding messages in hieroglyphs, using hieroglyphs to spell your name, interviewing for a job in ancient Egypt, or playing a “Trivial Pursuit” –style game about life on the Nile. Young children will want to crawl through a tomb shaft, and an automated light and audio “tour” of the Book of the Dead unlocks the mystery of ancient Egyptian religious beliefs. Discover Ancient Egypt is generously sponsored by Rockland Trust.

artworks.title: La bodega de mis sueños (The bodega of my dreams)
artworks.description: In this inaugural installation of public art on the museum’s façade, Cuban-American artist and educator Gabriel Sosa considers the stories of Spanish-speaking residents in Central Massachusetts, contemporary visual culture in downtown Fitchburg, and the complexities of the American Dream. La bodega de mis sueños (The bodega of my dreams) is a fictitious business that celebrates cultural heritage and collective histories while honoring the individual experiences of Spanish-speaking immigrants in Central Massachusetts. Sosa designed this installation to appear at first glance as an unassuming storefront; yet, couched within the expected advertisements for food products are postings for “esperanzas y añoranzas” (hopes and longings). These unexpectedly poignant elements in the storefront point to Sosa’s intention for viewers to pause and reflect upon the significance of the location.

artworks.title: Kaleidoscope: 100 Years of Collecting for Our Community
artworks.description: Kaleidoscope is the second in a series of exhibitions marking FAM’s Centennial, and features hundreds of artworks from our Permanent Collection, ranging across the globe, human history, and artistic media and movements. Featuring old favorites, new acquisitions, and rarely before seen artwork, Kaleidoscope juxtaposes it all, allowing visitors to create their own visual, psychological, intellectual, and spiritual meanings. The exhibition features over five-hundred artworks from the Museum’s Permanent Collection. Kaleidoscope is a celebration of both the power of art, and the variety and quality of the collection that we hold in trust for you. For more information please contact: Emily Mazzola, PhD., Curator, Fitchburg Art Museum, 185 Elm Street Fitchburg, MA 01420 emazzola@fitchburgartmuseum.org

artworks.title: FESTIVAL: A Celebration of African Art
artworks.description: FESTIVAL: A Celebration of African Art at the Fitchburg Art Museum is the first in a series of exhibitions honoring FAM’s Centennial. Drawing upon universal themes of life, death, power, love, and celebration, FESTIVAL presents highlights of FAM’s African Art collection organized around the concepts of Masquerades, Ceremonial Life, Ritual Life, and Domestic Life. From first millennium CE terracottas, to contemporary sculptures, FESTIVAL spans time and space, demonstrating both the breadth of FAM’s collection and the diversity of cultures and contexts across the African continent. Read the Fitchburg State University designed catalog for FESTIVAL: A Celebration of African Art at the Fitchburg Art Museum here .
